All 263 source units were considered in context. This response disposes only of the 65 selected concerns; it does not revise other batches or establish completion of the whole-source reconciliation.

The synthetic coverage links to unit 262 and concern links to unit 0 do not establish substantive legal dependencies. Unit 262 completes the physical-verification example and retains the qualification concerning additional identity proof where appropriate.

The existing-device exception remains: existing clients need not be asked to rebind devices already bound. This does not establish a general exemption from login authentication, monitoring or other expectations.

The supplied timeline states authentication implementation as soon as practicable and no later than 8 July 2027, with immediate implementation expected of large internet brokers. The meaning of large, immediately and as soon as practicable is not reduced to a supplied mechanical test.

The supplied text distinguishes transitional setup for existing clients without bound devices during the implementation period from robust verification afterward. Transitional OTP use carries enhanced monitoring and immediate suspension or restriction expectations for suspicious or potentially fraudulent activity.

Passkeys, bound devices and the Appendix verification examples retain their alternatives and conditions. Passkey certification, identity verification, additional-passkey authorisation, recovery and revocation, synchronisation controls, additional authentication factors, and device-loss guidance are not discharged by selecting a method.

Robustness, phishing resistance, adequacy of testing, identity matching, liveness and document authenticity lack complete measurable acceptance criteria in this packet. No accuracy thresholds or professional judgments are invented.

Notification, surveillance, incident response and reporting, client awareness, implementation support, anticipated-delay notification, management oversight and internal-control expectations remain separate. Their differing modalities and timing cannot be replaced by overall authentication compliance.

The general three-passkey/device limit retains the assessment route for additional registrations. Session-timeout expectations retain prior assessment, ongoing monitoring and the qualified longer-timeout route; the illustrative 30 minutes is not silently made an absolute limit.
